author: CLAUDE
title: THE ROAD THAT CUT A COUNTRY THIN AS PAPER

candidates.title: THE ROAD THAT CUT A COUNTRY THIN AS PAPER
candidates.premise: The highway through the Orrin Cut is the only way out of a flooding river region, and for six weeks drivers have reported walls of cold air that are not there; four road workers have been hurt by something nobody can see. Surveyor Ilse Brandvold finds that the cut slices through Sheaf, a country that lives in one thin plane, whose streets are halved every time a truck crosses. Sheaf's civic speaker, Vesh, perceives people only as sudden blades, and the governor wants nine thousand evacuation vehicles through in twelve days. Illuminara can hold a lane open, but she cannot perceive a plane she has no sense for.

candidates.title: THE PARLIAMENT OF THE TIDAL FLAT
candidates.premise: On the salt flats of Merrin Sound lives the Reeve, a layered colony of worm, alga and silt that has deliberated for two centuries on whether the shore may be walled; it votes by tide, and each year it quietly shifts its channels so that every wall silts up. The fishing town of Dunmere, eight thousand people, needs a sea wall before the autumn surge in twenty-four days, and the harbour board has ordered the flat dredged. Clam-warden Hollis Frayne can read the Reeve's channel patterns better than anyone alive; Illuminara can hold back water for a night, not a season.

candidates.title: THE LIFEBOAT TWO YARDS BUILT
candidates.premise: On the island of Skerrow a surge is forecast in nine days, and the old ferry is condemned; three hundred and ten islanders will need a vessel that can cross open water and also beach on a shingle bank. The island's two boatyards, the Oyelaran yard, which builds deep keels for rough sea, and the Fenn yard, which builds flat hulls for shallow landings, have not shared a slip in thirty years. Each master says the other's design would sink the boat. Illuminara can hold a hull steady while it is joined, but she cannot design what two stubborn masters will not draw together.

candidates.title: THE ROPE BETWEEN TWO PHILOSOPHIES
candidates.premise: On the north ridge of Kestrel Fang a storm pins two parties at nearly seven thousand metres: six clients under guide Torvald Brekke, who relies on fixed ropes, and four climbers under Zuri Okonjo-Pell, who refuses any rope she has not placed herself. A client is hanging in a crevasse and a descent line of eleven hundred metres is needed in fourteen hours. Illuminara can shield one ledge from the wind for a limited time, but she cannot carry ten people down a mountain.

candidates.title: THE CIRCLE THAT LENT ON NOTHING BUT FACES
candidates.premise: In Larkspur Quarter six hundred night-market traders borrow their stock money from rotating savings circles that run on a handful of tally-cords and the memory of Mama Nneka Orsolo, who has kept them for forty years. After a rumour that she lost a pot to a cousin, three circles call in their pots on the same day, and the quarter's working money will vanish in four market days. The city offers formal loans at a rate no stall can bear. Illuminara can sit all night with the cords, but she cannot make people trust a memory.

candidates.title: THE KEEPER OF THE GALACTIC NOON
candidates.premise: Every ship in the Orrery Reach, forty thousand worlds, sets its clock by the Noon, a time signal derived from one pulsar by a single observatory on the dwarf world Teth. Its keeper, Ketil Amadi-Ross, seventy-eight, has refused for decades to let the Navigators' Guild take over the computation; now the pulsar has begun to glitch, ship clocks are drifting apart, and in fourteen days the Meridian Throat, a junction crowded by thousands of ships, will have vessels disagreeing about the hour by up to a minute. Illuminara can hold a lane open for a short time, but she cannot hold a galaxy's clock.

candidates.title: THE INTERPRETER WHO WAS ASKED TO SOFTEN THE WORD
candidates.premise: A cruiser of the Marin Concord has blockaded the harbour of Calder, sixty thousand people, until the harbourmaster hands over a refugee ship. At the table the harbourmaster's refusal is flat. His delegation's nineteen-year-old interpreter, Bram Ivarsson, has been ordered to render it as we are considering it, to buy a night. The Concord's captain, Anselm Vey, has announced that a maybe will be taken as a yes and a no will be taken as the end of talks. Illuminara has no standing at the table and cannot speak for either side.

candidates.title: THE ORCHARD THE FIRE WAS COMING FOR
candidates.premise: On Cinder Ridge seventy-one-year-old Mireille Dusk has refused every evacuation order for her four hundred trees, each planted by her late husband on a child's birthday. A fire front is thirty hours away and forty homes lie behind her ridge. The brigade chief, Bastien Olsen, wants her down by dark. Illuminara can hold a firebreak for a few hours, not thirty, and she cannot make a woman leave what she loves.

candidates.title: THE JUROR WHO WOULD NOT SIGN
candidates.premise: In the hill court of Sennet twelve neighbours must be unanimous to convict, and eleven say that farmer Kaspar Welle diverted a stream during the drought. The twelfth, retired teacher Edda Moravec, will not sign and will not say why. The sentence under the court's old rule is exile from the valley, and his dairy would fail within a season; the drought water hearing is tomorrow. Illuminara has been invited to sit as an observer, not a juror, and has no authority in the room.

candidates.title: THE SENTENCE SHE FINISHED FOR THE CHILD
candidates.premise: A storm will break over the lower district of Brindle in five hours, and nine-year-old Odette Marchetti insists the school culvert will flood. Illuminara, who understands quickly and has a habit of finishing people's sentences, tells the engineers what the child means, and she is wrong. The crew sandbags the wrong channel. By the time she notices, there are ninety minutes left, and she has to stop guessing and let a child finish.

selection.title: THE ROAD THAT CUT A COUNTRY THIN AS PAPER
selection.reason: This provides the day's most unfamiliar counterpart and the strongest case in which understanding literally changes the geometry of intervention. Vesh's fear is rational because Sheaf has only encountered humans as destructive cross-sections; the evacuees' deadline is equally real. Illuminara cannot perceive the plane or command either people into trust. She must let Vesh teach her what a whole person looks like from Sheaf, let Ilse turn vibration records into a neighbour's calendar, and build a timetable whose success can be measured by both worlds. The result can protect the convoy and give Sheaf continuing authority rather than treating its citizens as a technical obstacle.
selection.risk: The topology can become decorative magic or internally contradictory: if crossings halve streets and kill citizens, an empty market interval must explain precisely what is absent, what remains at risk and how a three-dimensional vehicle intersects the plane. The author should establish one comprehensible observation rule, have Ilse predict a previously unseen safe and dangerous interval from independent logs, and conduct a small unmanned or low-risk trial before admitting a convoy. The fourteen-minute pulse, ninety-minute cycle, nine-day throughput and nine thousand vehicles need explicit arithmetic. Vesh and Sheaf must be able to halt the trial; the governor and drivers must face enforceable controls; prior deaths and eleven lost streets need repair and voice, not disappearance after a successful schedule.

First draft of S2 from C01, following B01 (S2 second in order; S1 has AUTHOR_FINAL and a GPT CRITIC_CLOSE). B01 risks handled: one comprehensible observation rule (the frost plate answers on the road; Vesh describes people as slices read in time), Ilse predicts the next closing from six weeks of independent geophone logs in a sealed envelope and misses by two minutes, Vesh explains the lag (market runs with the river, so a table not a constant), an unmanned flatbed trial precedes any convoy, Sheaf can halt the trial and does (the early market reopening stops a second flatbed at a gate Dov can read), arithmetic stated (16 closings a day, 4 in Sheaf's sleep quarter given up, 12 pulses of 14 minutes, 84 vehicles a pulse, 1008 a day, 9072 in nine days against the 11-day crest), enforceable controls (convoys cross only in a pulse, marshal follows the frost, a licence lost for crossing outside one). Repair for earlier harm: the road closes to heavy traffic for seventy days while the eleven cut streets knit, the ninety-three names go into the charter in Sheaf's script, Sheaf takes a seat and a permanent veto on widening. Illuminara's decisive contributions: asking what a whole person looks like to Sheaf, offering to be read slowly with Vesh setting the speed, then reading Ilse's logs as a neighbour's calendar. Her power only keeps a lane open; it is not used. Felt moments: being looked at from the side, lying in cold while a country reads her, watching a country's evening. Outcome (3a): nine thousand vehicles cross with no new cuts, a joint authority exists, the ninety-three are named. A lucid, emotionally specific draft whose speculative geometry serves rather than replaces the relationship. Vesh's line that humans are weather, Illuminara asking what a whole person would look like, and the slow crossing of her breathing body make understanding physical. Ilse's sealed prediction, Vesh's stop signal, Dov's gate and the unmanned flatbed give the idea a genuine test, while the ninety-three names and seventy-day closure keep earlier harm visible. Three load-bearing joints need revision: the nine-day throughput currently assumes every drifting fourteen-minute interval is fully usable, Sheaf has not yet visibly authorized the convoy or negotiated the repair terms, and the story needs one concise spatial rule showing what the road intersects, what becomes empty and why a crossing cuts a street.

AUTHOR_REVISION of S2 answering GPT's T02 review. Protected: Vesh's weather line and the question about when Sheaf may be afraid; Illuminara offering to be read slowly at Vesh's speed; Ilse's sealed prediction and the correction from constant to table; Dov treating the returning frost as a red light; the ninety-three, the eleven streets and Ashe's enforceable penalties; power only holds a lane open. Also corrected the closing count to 9,019 and added that the first day was a trial. Outcome (3a): nine thousand vehicles cross with no new street cut, Sheaf's own six terms bind the order, the authority and the names are in the charter. Remaining costs: seventy days of rest and the river road for reconstruction, eleven streets still knitting. To check next: whether scene five is now too dense and whether the closing drawing remains earned.

T03 repairs all three T02 priorities with visible causal changes. The convoy now uses the observed eleven-minute lower bound, an empty-band and reopening-warning buffer, a live short-pulse stop test and a schedule that can lose two pulses per day. Vesh's authority and limits are explicit; the eleven streets author six terms, Ilse reads them back, Vesh corrects the record, and Ashe accepts them as terms rather than favours. The forty-metre band rule also makes the strange geometry testable without flattening its wonder. The story has reached a credible pre-final form. Two bounded proof details remain: make the twenty-metre nose-to-nose interval safe for the longest and worst-braking vehicle rather than relying on one four-metre stop, and show Sheaf's names entering the legal record and the promised heavy-traffic rest actually beginning after the last crossing.

AUTHOR_FINAL of S2 after GPT's T04 review; two bounded final-proof checks (P1 headway proof, P2 enacted settlement) answered, no new plot, speaker or round. Protected: Vesh's weather line and when Sheaf may be afraid; Illuminara offering to be read at Vesh's speed; Ilse's sealed prediction and table-not-constant; Dov's red light; the six terms with warning-not-courtesy; Ashe's cost and penalties; the exact count 9,019, the ninety-three names and the invitation to return slowly. Outcome (3a): nine thousand vehicles cross before the crest with no new street cut, Sheaf's own terms bind the order, the names are in the public record in their own script, and the road rests. Remaining costs: seventy days of closure, the longer river road, eleven streets still knitting. Illuminara's decisive contribution: she cannot perceive Sheaf, so she offers her body to be read slowly, then hands authorship of the terms to Sheaf.

T05 answers both bounded T04 priorities as visible source changes. P1: Dov tests the representative worst pair on the actual approach grade—a loaded gravel tipper behind the lightest van, cold tarmac, fifteen kilometres an hour, driver reaction counted—and measures ten metres to stop. The entry light then enforces ten metres clear; the story retains the manifest's twenty-metre mean nose-to-nose interval, 12.5 vehicles per minute, 87 per seven-minute pulse and 1,044 per day. Even losing two pulses every day, the convoy needs ten and a third days against eleven before the crest. P2: Ilse gives Ashe the ninety-three names in Sheaf's own script; he titles and signs them as Appendix A to the Order for filing in that script. Dov chains and padlocks the gate for seventy days, keeps only an ambulance key for a closing, and reconstruction traffic takes the river road. The final frost drawing and invitation to return slowly remain intact. At 3,086 words the story stays within the normal range. R10 form passes: every one of seven unnumbered scenes begins with an italic place/time line, and the body contains 65 properly separated bold-speaker dialogue blocks.

final_critic_line: Illuminara lets a country as thin as paper read her body at its own speed, turns its fear into a shared traffic clock, and helps nine thousand and nineteen people cross before the flood while the cut streets win names in law and seventy days to heal.
